A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoisyToolBench, AwN and ToolEvaluator study, and all supplied pages, tables and figures are readable. Neither file contains an appendix, despite v1's references to one; those references provide no additional comparison evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original user-instruction analysis, AwN evaluations using two LLM engines in Tables 2–3, and human validation of ToolEvaluator on 50 cases.

after.justification: v3 reports the user-instruction analysis, evaluations using six LLM engines in Tables 2–3, and 50-case human validation of ToolEvaluator.

M1.justification: The AwN prompt and procedure for detecting ambiguity, requesting clarification and then invoking or refusing tools remain unchanged. ToolEvaluator retains its semantic-matching and judging workflow; the model substitutions concern evaluation settings.

E1.justification: Both retain the 1,000-query instruction study and benchmark construction from 200 ToolBench examples covering IMKI, IMR, IwE and IBTC. No additional dataset, domain or task scenario is documented.

E2.justification: CoT and DFSDT remain the evaluated comparison frameworks. The additional LLM engines instantiate the same comparisons with and without AwN; newly populated baseline metrics do not introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: The setup replaces gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 and gpt-4-0125 with gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, and adds GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini-1.5-Flash and Claude-3.5-Haiku. The judge changes from GPT-4 to GPT-4o. Baseline A2/A3 evaluation, explicitly excluded in v1, is added for IMKI, IMR and IwE.

E4.justification: v3 removes the Case Study subsection and Figure 4, which illustrated clarification after an API error caused by an incorrect product identifier. The 50-case evaluator-validation analysis remains; no new ablation or sensitivity analysis replaces the case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The random selection of 50 evaluator-validation cases remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace numerous scores and add four engine blocks plus previously omitted baseline A2/A3 entries. For example, GPT-3.5 CoT+AwN IMKI A2 changes from 0.56 to 0.44 under changed settings. Newly reported GPT-4o DFSDT IwE A2 is 0.06 without AwN and 0.46 with AwN. Cross-version changes are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions, proofs or derivations. The meanings of the five evaluation metrics and four instruction-error categories remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the instruction-error taxonomy, NoisyToolBench, AwN and ToolEvaluator, with improved tool use under unclear instructions. The six-engine evaluation adds support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v1 presents increased action counts as the cost of AwN and contrasts GPT-3.5's redundant questioning with GPT-4's efficiency. v3 instead emphasizes action-count reductions for GPT-4, DeepSeek and Gemini DFSDT, while qualifying extra costs and redundant questions for some agents. This substantially revises the efficiency interpretation; the two stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies updated engine identifiers and identifies GPT-4o as judge, but removes v1's explicit statement that baseline methods lack user interaction. The prompt excerpt, annotation procedure, unspecified default settings and promise of future code/data release remain; no new access location or detailed hyperparameters are supplied.

R1.justification: The Learning to Ask discussion adds Rao and Daumé III (2018), Kuhn et al. (2022, CLAM), and Andukuri et al. (2024, STaR-GATE). The positioning against Qian et al. and the broader tool-learning literature otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title terminology to LLM Agents, updates authors and affiliations, numbers sections, rearranges the prompt presentation, rewrites the results discussion and shortens the conclusion. Most explanatory prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document is substantially reformatted. Tables 2–3 expand from two to six model blocks; Table 2 removes empty IBTC A2/A3 columns, and Table 3 becomes a compact single-column table with vertical model labels. Figure 4 is removed, while Figures 1–3 retain their content with changed sizing or placement.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important evidential gap: Table 2 now reports baseline API-call and final-answer accuracy that v1 explicitly omitted, enabling direct assessment of successful execution. Broader engine testing and the revised cost discussion substantially strengthen assessment of AwN's benefits and exceptions. These gains outweigh losing the illustrative case and baseline-interaction disclosure, although reproducibility and uncertainty reporting remain limited. Changed checkpoints and judge prevent treating cross-version score differences as performance gains.
